title: Solar Power Design and Installation Basics
desc: Learn to size, design and plan a small solar system with correct safety, cost, layout and handover.
outcomes: Explain how panels, inverters and batteries work together.
Size a small system from a load list.
Produce a design pack and handover sheet.
task: Design a small rooftop solar system for a practice home or shop, with load list, size, layout, safety plan, cost, payback and handover sheet.
condition: A computer, a spreadsheet, a floor plan or satellite view, two peers and a licensed electrician mentor. Installation on live wiring is done only by licensed people.
standard: Load list and size are correct; roof and shade checks are done; protective devices and earthing are listed; cost and payback shown; a licensed person signs the design; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Trainee electricians, technicians, small shop owners, community energy workers.
evidence: load list, sizing sheet, layout drawing, safety plan, cost sheet, handover sheet
modules: How a solar system works
Understand
Panels turn sunlight into direct current electricity; an inverter changes it to the alternating current your appliances use.
Types: grid-tied, off-grid with batteries, and hybrid.
Parts: panels, mounting, inverter, cables, breakers, meter, optional battery.
Energy units: kWh = kW x hours.
Output depends on sun, temperature, shade, tilt and dirt.
A grid-tied system sends extra daytime power to the network and draws from it at night. A hybrid system also charges a battery for backup.
Draw a block diagram of a hybrid system and label each part.
All parts named and the energy flow is correct.
Load list
Apply
Know what you use before sizing anything.
List each appliance with watts and hours used per day.
Add up daily watt-hours; check against bills.
Cut waste first with efficient lamps, fans and cooling.
Note peak load and any large motor starts.
A shop uses 12 kWh a day. Efficient lights save 1.5 kWh, so the system is sized for 10.5 kWh.
Make a load list for a practice building with at least ten loads.
Totals are correct and checked against a bill.
Site survey
Analyse
The roof and its surroundings decide the output.
Check orientation, tilt, shading, roof strength and space.
Find sun hours per day in your place from public data.
Look for safe access and fall protection.
Photograph the roof and the electrical panel.
A water tank shades part of the roof in the afternoon and would cost 8 per cent of annual output. The panels are moved to another section.
Do a mock survey from photos and write a findings sheet.
Findings listed with fixes.
Sizing the system
Apply
Match supply to load with a transparent calculation.
Panel kW = daily kWh / (sun hours x system efficiency).
Choose an inverter slightly below panel kW.
Battery size = backup hours x load / (depth of discharge).
Check voltage and current limits.
12 kWh a day, 5 sun hours and 0.75 efficiency gives 12 / (5 x 0.75) = 3.2 kW of panels, about eight 400 W panels.
Size a system for your load list and show all steps.
Calculations are correct with units.
Electrical protection and earthing
Apply
Safety devices are not optional.
Fuses or breakers on each string and on the AC side, surge protection, isolators and earthing.
Correct cable size, colour and routing.
Label every device and the main switch.
Only a licensed electrician connects to the grid or home wiring.
A DC isolator is added near the inverter and a label at the main board reads "Solar supply – isolate both sources".
List all protective devices for your design.
Licensed mentor approves the list.
Safety on site
Evaluate
Heights and live parts demand a safe method.
Fall protection, safe ladders and PPE.
Panels make power in daylight: treat all wiring as live.
Lock-out and tag-out; weather checks.
Never work alone.
A crew stops roof work on a windy afternoon and reschedules for the next morning.
Write a site safety plan.
Plan names hazards, controls and who is responsible.
Cost and payback
Evaluate
Know the real numbers before you decide.
Costs: panels, inverter, mounting, cable, labour, permits, insurance.
Savings: bills avoided or income from export; maintenance costs.
Payback and cost per kWh over system life.
Test with price rises and shading losses.
Cost 2,10,000 INR; saving 32,000 INR per year; payback 6.6 years.
Build a cost sheet with currency shown.
Maths correct and assumptions listed.
Design pack and handover
Create
Hand over a pack that someone else can understand and maintain.
Single-line diagram, layout drawing, specifications and warranty.
Train the owner on cleaning, monitoring and shut-down.
Schedule checks every six months.
Keep records.
The owner receives a one-page guide with shut-down steps, an emergency contact and a cleaning schedule.
Produce a design pack and handover sheet.
Pack is signed by a licensed person.
quiz: What converts DC to AC?
Inverter. (Covered in module 1: System parts. To pass that module: All parts named.)
kWh equals?
kW times hours. (Covered in module 2: Load list. To pass that module: Totals correct.)
Name a shading effect.
Output drops. (Covered in module 3: Site survey. To pass that module: Findings listed with fixes.)
Panel sizing formula?
Daily kWh / (sun hours x efficiency). (Covered in module 4: Sizing. To pass that module: Steps shown.)
Name two protective devices.
Breaker and surge protector. (Covered in module 5: Electrical protection and earthing. To pass that module: Licensed mentor approves.)
Who may wire live circuits?
Licensed electricians. (Covered in module 6: Safety on site. To pass that module: Plan names hazards and controls.)
Why label everything?
Safe maintenance and emergency. (Covered in module 7: Cost and payback. To pass that module: Maths correct; currency shown.)
Payback formula?
Cost / yearly saving. (Covered in module 8: Design pack and handover. To pass that module: Pack signed by a licensed person.)
Why cut waste first?
Smaller, cheaper system. (Covered in module 8: Design pack and handover. To pass that module: Pack signed by a licensed person.)
Are panels live in daylight?
Yes. (Covered in module 8: Design pack and handover. To pass that module: Pack signed by a licensed person.)

ladder: System parts

L1: learner can name solar parts. Focus module: System parts (Understand, 3 h). Panels make direct current; the inverter converts it. Key points: Types: grid-tied, off-grid, hybrid. Parts: panels, mounting, inverter, wiring, breakers, meter, optional battery. Energy: kWh = kW x hours.

Teach: open with the worked example. A grid-tied system sends extra power to the network. Then set the activity: Draw a block diagram. Mark against the standard: All parts named. Check at this level: What converts DC to AC? Model answer: Inverter. Diagram.
Load list

L2: learner knows safety basics. Focus module: Load list (Apply, 4 h). Know what you use. Key points: List each appliance: watts, hours a day. Add daily watt-hours; check bills. Cut waste first, with efficient lamps and fans.

Teach: open with the worked example. A shop uses 12 kWh a day; efficient lights save 1.5 kWh. Then set the activity: Make a load list. Mark against the standard: Totals correct. Check at this level: kWh equals? Model answer: kW times hours. Safety.
Site survey

L3: learner can make a load list. Focus module: Site survey (Analyse, 4 h). Roof and shade decide output. Key points: Orientation, tilt, shade, roof strength, space. Sun hours per day in your place. Safe roof access and fall protection.

Teach: open with the worked example. A shade from a tank costs 8% in the afternoon; panels are moved. Then set the activity: Do a mock survey from a photo. Mark against the standard: Findings listed with fixes. Check at this level: Name a shading effect. Model answer: Output drops. Load list.
Sizing

L4: learner can size a small system. Focus module: Sizing (Apply, 5 h). Match supply to load. Key points: Panel kW = daily kWh / (sun hours x system efficiency). Choose inverter slightly below panel kW. Battery size from backup hours and depth of discharge.

Teach: open with the worked example. 12 kWh a day, 5 sun hours, 0.75 efficiency: about 3.2 kW of panels. Then set the activity: Size your system. Mark against the standard: Steps shown. Check at this level: Panel sizing formula? Model answer: Daily kWh / (sun hours x efficiency). Size.
Electrical protection and earthing

L5: learner can design protection and cost. Focus module: Electrical protection and earthing (Apply, 5 h). Safety is not optional. Key points: Fuses, breakers, surge protection, isolators and earthing. Correct cable size and colours. Label everything.

Teach: open with the worked example. A DC isolator is added near the inverter. Then set the activity: List protective devices. Mark against the standard: Licensed mentor approves. Check at this level: Name two protective devices. Model answer: Breaker and surge protector. Protection.
Cost and payback

L6: learner can lead a small crew. Focus module: Cost and payback (Evaluate, 4 h). Know the real numbers. Key points: Panels, inverter, mounting, cable, labour, permits. Savings per year from bills; maintenance. Payback and lifetime cost per kWh.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cost 210,000 INR; saving 32,000 INR a year; payback 6.6 years. Then set the activity: Build a cost sheet. Mark against the standard: Maths correct; currency shown. Check at this level: Who may wire live circuits? Model answer: Licensed electricians. Crew.
Design pack and handover

L7: learner can audit a design. Focus module: Design pack and handover (Create, 4 h). Hand over a clear pack. Key points: Single-line diagram, layout, specs, warranty. Teach the owner cleaning and safety. Plan checks every six months.

Teach: open with the worked example. The owner receives a one-page guide with shut-down steps. Then set the activity: Produce a design pack and handover sheet. Mark against the standard: Pack signed by a licensed person. Check at this level: Why label everything? Model answer: Safe maintenance and emergency. Peer audit.
